subject: Maths
title: Finding a shorter side
subtitle: Pythagoras' Theorem · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can use Pythagoras' theorem to find a shorter side of a right-angled triangle.

key_vocab.definition: When the hypotenuse and one shorter side are known, rearrange Pythagoras to find the other: a² = c² − b².

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can use Pythagoras' theorem to find a shorter side of a right-angled triangle.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: hypotenuse -- When the hypotenuse and one shorter side are known, rearrange Pythagoras to find the other: a² = c² − b².

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Rearrange a² + b² = c² to a² = c² − b², then take the square root.
a = √(c² − b²)
Subtract known shorter side squared from hypotenuse squared

Key examples:
  ✓ c = 13, b = 5: a = √(169 − 25) = √144 = 12  (subtract then root)
  ✓ c = 10, b = 6: a = √(100 − 36) = √64 = 8  (rearranged formula)
  ✓ c = 15, b = 9: a = √(225 − 81) = √144 = 12  (Pythagorean triple)
  ✗ c = 13, b = 5: a = √(169 + 25)  (must subtract, not add)
  ✗ a = c − b = 13 − 5 = 8  (must square first, then subtract)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – integer answer
  Find side a if c = 10 and b = 8.
  a² = c² − b² = 100 − 64 = 36
  a = √36
  a = 6
  a = 6
  (Always square both known sides first, then subtract.)

Example 2 – non-integer answer
  Find side a if c = 9 and b = 5.
  a² = 81 − 25 = 56
  a = √56
  a = 7.48 (2 d.p.)
  a = 7.48
  (If the answer is not a perfect square, round appropriately.)

sections.title: Finding a (integer answers)
sections.content:
Find the missing shorter side.

(a) c = 5, b = 3
(b) c = 13, b = 12
(c) c = 15, b = 12
(d) c = 25, b = 7

sections.title: Finding a (decimal answers)
sections.content:
Find the missing side to 1 d.p.

(a) c = 8, b = 5
(b) c = 12, b = 7
(c) c = 10, b = 4
(d) c = 20, b = 11

sections.title: In context
sections.content:
Solve each problem.

(a) Ladder 10 m, reaches 8 m up wall. Distance from wall?
(b) Kite string 26 m, horizontal distance 10 m. Height?
(c) Ship sails: total journey 17 km, east 15 km. North?
(d) Slide 13 m, platform height 5 m. Ground distance?

sections.title: Mixed triangles
sections.content:
Find x in each right-angled triangle.

(a) Hypotenuse 17, one side x, other side 15
(b) Hypotenuse 26, one side x, other side 24
(c) Hypotenuse 20, one side x, other side 12
(d) Hypotenuse 29, one side x, other side 21

sections.title: Problem solving
sections.content:
Solve each problem. Round to 1 d.p. where needed.

(a) Right triangle: hypotenuse 14, one leg 6. Other leg?
(b) Rectangle diagonal 15, width 9. Length?
(c) Isosceles: equal sides 10, base 16. Height?
(d) Right triangle: hypotenuse 11, one leg 7. Other leg?
(e) Square diagonal 8. Side length?

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ To find a shorter side, rearrange to a² = c² − b²
✗ a = c − b gives the missing side
✓ The hypotenuse is always the longest side in a right-angled triangle
✗ a² = c² + b² when finding a shorter side
✓ If the answer is not exact, round to an appropriate degree of accuracy
